text:
priya: Heads up — we're seeing SLO degradation for gpu-provisioning in eu-west-1. Warm pool attach fail rate jumped ~30% over the last 12m. Keystore decrypt errors in the attach path.
ben: Confirmed. Logs show repeated 403s from keystore decrypt service: `AccessDenied: Condition 'aws:SourceVpc' mismatch` at attach step.
kai: That sounds like the IAM condition PR we merged last night that added `aws:SourceVpc` to the privnet-keystore role. @infra-iam?
nora: Also rolled the default-deny firewall on privnet subnets this morning (cf. the rollout thread). Could be a two-factor failure: IAM + new firewall rules.
ops-bot: [ALERT] gpu-provisioner-eu-west: provisioning_latency_p95 crossed 2.5s -> alert fired (rule: gpuprov.latency.p95 > 2s).
priya: Paste of failing line from provisioner logs: `attach_keystore: decrypt() -> 403 AccessDenied (sts:AssumeRole) role=privnet-keystore region=eu-west-1 src_vpc=vpce-0a12b3c4`
ben: Quick repro from bastion -> curl to keystore endpoint returns 403 unless we spoof SourceVpc header. So IAM condition is enforced.
kai: Proposed mitigation steps: 1) rollback IAM condition change (fast) 2) open short-lived firewall exception for privnet-keystore endpoint from gpu nodes 3) enable fallback to keystore replica in us-west for attaches (as a degraded but safe fallback). Which order preferred?
priya: Rollback IAM change first — that's the quickest to get kube warmpool healthy. If that's no-go, firewall exception next. Need to avoid mass node ejection.
nora: We should also capture audit logs before changing policies. Create a temporary retention bucket and forward current keystore access logs there (low effort).
ben: I'll prepare a rollback PR for the IAM condition. Patch will remove the `Condition: {'StringEquals': {'aws:SourceVpc': 'vpce-...'}}` block.
priya: Ben, can you also include a narrow allow for `sts:AssumeRole` from the provisioner role as a stopgap? Keep it scoped to `arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/gpu-provisioner`.
ben: Yep. Drafting now.
kai: Nora, can you open the firewall exception for keystore endpoint from the gpu-subnet CIDR (10.200.0.0/18) while we roll? Keep TTL 15m and log.
nora: On it. Creating temporary rule: `allow tcp 443 from 10.200.0.0/18 to vpce-xxxx (privnet-keystore)` with tag `sre-keystore-fix`. Will add audit log forwarding to `sre-keystore-audit`.
priya: Linking playbook snippet for rollback (copy/paste):
```
# rollback IAM condition
aws iam update-assume-role-policy --role-name privnet-keystore --policy-document file://keystore-trust-rollback.json
# sample trust update removes aws:SourceVpc condition
```
ben: PR up: https://git.redwood/infra/iam/pulls/847 — moving to rollback. Will request infra-iam + security approval for emergency revert.
deploy-bot: Deployment started: iam/privnet-keystore rollback candidate -> staging (deploy id: dpl-20260321-1228). No config drift detected.
ops-bot: Metric update: gpu-warmpool.attach_success_rate eu-west-1 -> 0.72 (was 0.58) after IAM rollback deploy (2m).
ben: Firewall exception applied (rule id fr-789) for 15m, logging enabled.
priya: After both rollback + firewall exception, attach success back to 0.98 in last 4m. Good.
kai: I'll kick a small canary of 10 nodes to ensure nothing else regresses.
nora: Forwarded keystore audit logs to `sre-keystore-audit` bucket — preserved pre-rollback window.
priya: Nice work. Next actions: write up postmortem, lock down a safer deployment flow for keystore IAM conditions (staged tests + canary), and add an automated smoke check in eu-west before firing default-deny.
ben: Agreed. I'll add a gating test in CI that simulates privnet VPC header check.
priya: Closing this thread as service recovered. Will create postmortem draft in #postmortems and tag infra/security. :white_check_mark:
